title: Allocation Stands At ₹705.11 Crore In 2023-24, ₹539.44 Crore In 2024-25 And ₹557.42 Crore In 2025-26, Amounting To A Total Allocation Of ₹1,801.97 Crores Over The Three-Year Period Under WELFARE SCHEMES FOR SENIOR CITIZENS
subtitle: No Pending Applications Under SHREYAS-SC; NO REDUCTION IN DE-ADDICTION CENTRE ALLOCATION DURING LAST THREE YEARS
body_text:
The Central Government has clarified the status of scholarship applications and unpaid scholarship dues for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Persons with Disabilities (PwDs), while also providing details of budget allocations for de-addiction centres and welfare schemes for senior citizens.
In a written reply to Dr. Menaka Guruswamy in the Rajya Sabha , the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale stated that the Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes & Others and the Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students are Centrally Sponsored Schemes that are open-ended and demand-driven.
He stated that the scholarships are released through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of beneficiaries adding that the release of the Central share is contingent upon the concerned State Government or UT Administration releasing its share and uploading the finally verified paid data on the National Scholarship Portal.
Under the Central Sector Scheme of Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme for SCs ( SHREYAS-SC ), the Government stated that no scholarship application is pending and there are no unpaid scholarship dues .
On allocations for de-addiction centres, the Government clarified that there has been no reduction in budget allocation during the last three years .
For welfare schemes for senior citizens , the allocation stood at ₹ 705.11 crore in 2023-24, ₹ 539.44 crore in 2024-25 and ₹ 557.42 crore in 2025-26, amounting to a total allocation of ₹ 1,801.97 crores over the three-year period.
The Government further informed that the Prime Minister Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India for OBCs and others ( PM-YASASVI ) comprises four sub-schemes— Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top-Class Education in Colleges and Top-Class Education in Schools for OBC, EBC and DNT students.
The Pre-Matric and Post-Matric components are Centrally Sponsored Schemes, with processing, verification, sanction and disbursement undertaken by the respective State Governments and UT Administrations, while the Central Government releases funds to the States and UTs. The Top-Class Education in Schools and Top-Class Education in Colleges components are Central Sector Schemes.
With regard to students with disabilities, the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) is implementing the Central Sector “Scholarship Scheme for Students with Disabilities”. Applications received under the scheme are processed in accordance with the prevailing scheme guidelines, subject to fulfilment of prescribed eligibility conditions and submission of complete applications. Sanction and release of scholarships are undertaken continuously during the academic year.
The Government's response highlights the demand-driven nature of key scholarship schemes, the DBT-based mechanism for scholarship disbursement, and the continuous processing of eligible applications under the respective schemes.

enrichment.summary: In a Rajya Sabha written reply, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment stated that no scholarship applications or dues are pending under SHREYAS-SC, and that there has been no reduction in de-addiction centre funding over the last three years. It also disclosed budget allocations for welfare schemes for senior citizens: ₹705.11 crore (2023-24), ₹539.44 crore (2024-25), and ₹557.42 crore (2025-26), totaling ₹1,801.97 crore. The reply also detailed the structure of scholarship schemes for SCs, OBCs (PM-YASASVI), and persons with disabilities.
enrichment.context:
These schemes fall under the broader ambit of social justice and welfare architecture aimed at Scheduled Castes, OBCs, Persons with Disabilities, and senior citizens. Pre-Matric and Post-Matric scholarships for SCs are Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) that are open-ended and demand-driven, meaning funds are released based on actual eligible beneficiaries rather than a fixed cap, and disbursed via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to reduce leakages. PM-YASASVI, launched to consolidate scholarship support for OBC, EBC and De-notified Tribes (DNT) students, has both CSS components (Pre/Post-Matric, implemented via states) and Central Sector components (Top-Class Education, implemented directly by the Centre) — this distinction matters for understanding Centre-State fiscal responsibility in welfare delivery. Welfare schemes for senior citizens include initiatives like the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens, Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, and Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), addressing India's rapidly ageing population under the National Policy on Older Persons framework. De-addiction centres, run by NGOs under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction, are important given the government's fight against substance abuse.

Such parliamentary replies are a key source of updated data for aspirants tracking social sector governance, DBT reforms, and Centre-State scheme implementation dynamics, though this particular release mainly consolidates administrative clarifications rather than announcing new policy.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding PM-YASASVI scheme:
1. It is meant for OBC, EBC and DNT students.
2. All four components of the scheme are Centrally Sponsored Schemes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: PM-YASASVI covers OBC, EBC and DNT students through four sub-schemes, but only Pre-Matric and Post-Matric are Centrally Sponsored Schemes; Top-Class Education in Schools and Colleges are Central Sector Schemes. Hence only statement 1 is correct.

prelims_questions.question: The scholarship amounts under schemes like Post-Matric Scholarship for SC students are disbursed to beneficiaries through which mechanism?
options: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that scholarships are released through DBT into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of beneficiaries, contingent on state governments releasing their matching share.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in improving the efficiency of scholarship schemes for socially and economically disadvantaged groups in India. What challenges remain in its implementation under Centrally Sponsored Schemes?

India's ageing population necessitates robust welfare mechanisms for senior citizens. Critically examine the adequacy of current government schemes and budgetary allocations in addressing the needs of the elderly.
